text: In 13C metabolic flux analysis, what is the key distinction between an isotopologue and an isotopomer?
choices: Isotopologues differ in the position of labeled atoms; isotopomers differ only in the total count of labeled atoms
Isotopologues and isotopomers are interchangeable terms for the same concept
Isotopologues differ in total number of heavy atoms and are measured by MS; isotopomers share the same heavy-atom count but differ in position, distinguished by NMR
Isotopologues can only be measured by NMR, and isotopomers only by mass spectrometry
explanation: Isotopologues are molecules with the same molecular formula but a different number of heavy atoms, which mass spectrometry can resolve by mass; isotopomers share the same formula and the same heavy-atom count but differ in which positions carry the label, which requires NMR to distinguish since MS cannot tell position-isomers apart by mass alone. The first option swaps these definitions, the second wrongly claims they are synonyms, and the last option reverses which technique measures which property.
